summary: LibreOffice, from the inside: a bridge to Writer and Calc through UNO. workbench/office_bridge.py (Kernel side) owns a headless LibreOffice of her own (private profile with macros off and her name on lock files, private pipe, own process group, one at a time, ended after each piece of work, crash leftovers swept) and talks JSON lines to workbench/office_uno_helper.py, run under the system python3 that has uno. Six Kernel operations: libreoffice.status, .read, .find, .prepare (read) and libreoffice.replace, .cell (approve). A change is made only at the revision the plan read, only where the passage is in exactly the places named, never on a document the owner has open in LibreOffice (lock file), never while her work is held (HALT); the version before is kept, the save holds off a suspend (sleep_held), the saved file is read back directly (content.xml parsed here, not by LibreOffice) and compared paragraph by paragraph or cell by cell, and the new revision is recorded through revisions.record (L4). Checks for assignments (K1) look for an effect before making it again and verify it after; K2's slots office.read/office.edit are filled through a guarded import; offer_update() gives K4 the step, or the change as prepared text when LibreOffice is not here. Smoke on Rail Demo: 28 of 28 checks printed PASS.

decisions: Two halves: Graphite's venv cannot import uno, so the UNO side is a stdlib-only helper script run as /usr/bin/python3 -I -B (found in this order: GRAPHITE_UNO_PYTHON, LibreOffice's own program/python, /usr/bin/python3, python3 on PATH; each tried with 'import uno'). When none can, the reason says python3-uno is missing (Debian package python3-uno, in the 1.0 System set).

Headless only, one owned LibreOffice per piece of work (about 3 s each here, most of it LibreOffice starting), never a visible window: DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY are removed from its environment. native_sessions.py's visible Calc sessions are untouched; the ownership model is the same (own profile, own process group, ended in every case). A persistent profile folder in the Kernel's state (.ledger/office-bridge/profile) is reused for speed; its settings file is rewritten each start so macros stay off and no recent-documents list is kept.

Scopes: the four reads are 'read'; libreoffice.replace and libreoffice.cell are 'approve' (a change to the owner's document through another program is his word by its name). In an assignment (K1) such a step is authorised by its own name with its arguments fixed; so K4 plans the update step after the value is checked (offer_update takes the checked value as a literal whose origin is the calculation page at its revision). files_service.may_change is applied as for files.write.

Edits are limited to OpenDocument files (.odt passages, .ods value cells) because the verification reads content.xml directly; .docx/.xlsx/.doc/.rtf are read through LibreOffice only. A cell holding a formula is never overwritten; formulas that read the cell are reported as worked again.

Verification compares every paragraph of the saved file (read directly) with the paragraphs before with the passage replaced; LibreOffice's count of the passage must equal the direct reader's count, else nothing is saved. A save that does not verify is still recorded as a revision (it is on disk) and reported 'not verified', never hidden.

Revisions are recorded through depths.record with how='full program' and program='LibreOffice (Kasandra)', so the board says 'revision 2, saved in LibreOffice (Kasandra)'; the revision before is recorded as revision 1 when there was none.

The owner's lock: a .~lock.<name># that is not hers (hers carries 'Kasandra (Graphite)' and the office-bridge profile) refuses any change with the reason; a lock of hers left by a crash is cleared under the bridge's own lock. Reading a document he has open is allowed and says it reads the file as last saved.

Without the interface: reads of .odt/.ods fall back to the direct read and say so; changes are refused with "LibreOffice's interface is not available here: <why>"; libreoffice.prepare (a read) and offer_update() give the change as prepared text. GRAPHITE_LIBREOFFICE=off turns the bridge off (used by the smoke to show the fallback).
No window changes: nothing new is drawn (the brief allowed this; a step's receipt reaches her column through K1/P1's ACTIVE WORK and K2's receipts), so no frames were taken.
libreoffice.status is not added to activity's observer list (it is not on a paint path); reads are ordinary events.
findings_for_the_coordinator: K2 is in main, not in this tree: office_bridge._join() fills tools_registry slots 'office.read' (libreoffice.read, .find, .prepare) and 'office.edit' (libreoffice.replace, .cell) with available=office_bridge.available and the callable names, through a guarded import, and installs its own per-operation checks in assignments.CHECKS (fill's single check= would put one check on both edit operations, so it is not passed). The smoke ran with main's tools_registry.py and assignments.py copied into the throwaway copy only: slots filled, receipts 'dispatched' then 'verified' for the step.

Because tools_registry.WRITES_FILES is computed when tools_registry is imported (before the slot is filled), K2's holding() does not hold a sleep lock for the libreoffice operations; the bridge holds session_power.sleep_held around its own save, so nothing is lost. K2's unmet() returns [] for the office family; the bridge's Check.prepare enforces the preconditions.

Merge order: the registration lines sit right after L4's depths lines in engineering_kernel.py and engineering_cli.py; the registry record was regenerated here (863 operations) and needs the usual regeneration at merge.

Inside 'unshare --pid' the smoke's python is PID 1 and does not reap orphans, so a LibreOffice child shows as a zombie; the bridge counts zombies as gone (it scans /proc for live members of its process group), which also keeps the close at about 2 s on a normal system.

X1 can use office_bridge.place_examples(kernel) to put the invented report and sheet in Files/Rail Demo/ and office_bridge.offer_update(kernel, owner, path, '3.0 W', '3.6 W', basis={'kind': 'RECORD', 'id': page, 'rev': rev}) for the step (or the prepared text).
not_done: Not tested in the owner's sense; nothing ran on the ThinkPad. Only the smoke script ran, offscreen in this container with LibreOffice 24.2.7 and the system Python 3.13 with python3-uno.
No visible-session bridge (driving a LibreOffice window the owner sees); by the brief her work is headless and the owner's windows are never driven.
No edits of .docx/.xlsx (read only through LibreOffice); no passage in headers, footers, footnotes or frames (only the body text and its tables are verified).
No guide entry or window control for the bridge (X2 writes the guide; K4/X1 wire it into the plan and the day).
release_note: Kasandra can now work inside LibreOffice Writer and Calc through LibreOffice's own interface: she reads a document's paragraphs and tables or a sheet's cells, finds a passage, replaces it or sets a value cell, saves, and calls it done only after she has read the saved file back and recorded its new revision. Her LibreOffice is headless and her own (it never shows a window, never runs a macro), each change is yours to approve by name, a document you have open in LibreOffice is never edited behind your back, and without LibreOffice or python3-uno she says why and offers the change as prepared text.
